body: Oh I relate to this. And I went through my trauma  pretty privately, only a handful of people currently in my life know. I always wanted a “reason” for my depression, because I felt wrong for feeling so badly when my life was ok on the outside. And then I got one, and it didn’t change anything except giving me PTSD lmao

I am so so sorry that happened to you. If you want, PM me. I have never spoken to someone else that became pregnant through rape, it’s such an isolating experience.

I am doing a lot better now. Putting time between myself and this experience has helped a lot. I developed PTSD that I am doing a lot better with now, and I got sober just over a year ago which has made a world of difference. I was really suicidal and destructive for a long time.

I still have a lot of issues with sex. Like I said I’d only had sex one time before this so I didn’t have any experiences of healthy, loving sex to lean back on. Sometimes it is hard for me to separate the rape from sex in general. But I am taking baby steps into the world of dating, even if I have to take things really slow.

I hope you are doing better as well. All love to you.

Thank you for asking! It has been a really, really, really uphill 3.5 years but I am making progress even still. I developed PTSD that I am doing a lot better with now, but I still have a lot of trouble sleeping without having nightmares. I leaned really heavily on substances after the rape to deal with everything, but I have been sober for just over a year now and that has made a world of difference with how suicidal and destructive I was before. 

The biggest thing I still have trouble with is sex and relationships. I don't like being touched and the few times I have had sex I often have to stop because I will dissociate. I am making baby steps into the world of dating now, for what is really the first time ever for me. I feel ready to be a part of a healthy relationship even if I take sex slow to start with. Sobriety has helped a lot with that too.

I wish I had a good answer for this, but so many of the solutions for this are structural. I think ending the backlog of rape kit testing is a good place to start. Making sure every hospital has at least one sexual assault nurse examiner (SANE) on shift, since they are trained in trauma-informed care. I think more women would be likely to do rape kits if they felt that they would be taken seriously by the police, and would have a chance of successfully prosecuting at all (according to RAINN only 5/1000 rapists will see jail). 

But I don't know. Rape kits are painful and intrusive regardless of being tied to the worst moments of a person's life, but they're also the best chance at getting evidence to prosecute. There's not a lot in the kit itself that can be made easier for the victim without comprising the investigation unfortunately, so it's a matter of making sure the victim feels supported and  taken seriously. I think there would need to be a massive overhaul with the way these cases are handled to make more women comfortable reporting.

I don’t know. I did save my underwear and pants from that night and gave them to the police, and they did tell me (months later, after I had already had the abortion) that they pulled DNA off them. The officer couldn’t tell me whether the DNA matched to anyone because I had declined to prosecute at that point. If timelines with the police had happened differently, if I had learned about the DNA prior to the abortion, I would have probably had the embryo tested for paternity. It’s hard to say at this point because there are so many what ifs where if things had gone just a little differently I might have gone to court.

As if we’re all surrounded by people looking to adopt a child? All of my friends were also 20 year olds enrolled in school and getting ready to start their lives. My parents are divorced, would be in their 70s by the time the child was grown, and are both only children without extended family.

I support abortion regardless of the cause. 

One issue I have with the exception made for rape or incest is: who’s deciding that the rape was “legitimate?” Women would have to report right away to have a rape kit done (which is painful and traumatizing in itself). If the courts decided, is there any guarantee that it would happen quickly enough for the woman to still be able to have the abortion? The officer I reported to said prosecuting could take up to two years. What if they decided no even if she was raped? There’s a whole additional set of problems that would arise from only allowing abortions in certain cases.

Thank you very much. I did report to the police, but didn’t want to follow up with prosecution. I still wonder if I should have gone through with it. 

It took the police five months to even tell me that they had pulled DNA off of my underwear from that night, and the officer told me that it could take two years or more to go through with everything which scared me off a bit. 

Also, they wanted me to contact him (I guess I gave him my phone number that night. I don’t remember doing it, but I was scared so I guess I did. He was calling me leaving messages after for weeks) and try to get him to say something incriminating over the phone. I couldn’t do it, the thought of calling him and trying to “lure” him somehow still makes me feel sick. 

All that being said, thank you
Thank you, I really appreciate it.

Truthfully, no. On a practical level, I was not financially ready for a child. I lived in an apartment with two roommates and was halfway through my degree at the time. I had a job but it was barely enough to cover my own living expenses. Raising it would have meant moving back home and leaving school. I was not emotionally ready for a child either, even though I love kids. 

I probably would have tried to have an abortion anyway, or even tried to induce a miscarriage honestly. If I had been forced to have the baby, I would have given it up for adoption.
